info.title: codecharter
info.description: Deterministic code quality analysis for .NET, built on Roslyn. Write rules in a LINQ-like DSL, store them as .ccr files, and analyze a solution or project from the command line with CI-friendly exit codes. Restores versioned rule profiles from the CodeCharter portal, runs rule specs, gates line coverage, and ships an MCP server so AI coding tools can analyze on demand. Documentation: https://codecharter.tools. Requires a valid CodeCharter license or API key at runtime.

options.name: --output
options.description: Output format, optionally with a destination as format:path. Formats: console, github-annotations (stdout, no path), json, sarif. Repeatable to emit several formats from one run, e.g. --output github-annotations --output json:codecharter.json --output sarif:codecharter.sarif. File formats (json, sarif) require a path when combined; at most one stdout format per run. Defaults to console.

options.description: Exit code 1 if any violation at this level: error, warn, info

options.description: Disable ANSI color codes [default: False]

options.description: Show detailed progress [default: False]

options.name: --progress
options.description: Show live progress (per-project and per-rule) on stderr while analyzing. Can be combined with --verbose. [default: False]

options.name: --workspace-root
options.description: Strip this path prefix from file paths (used with github-annotations format)

options.name: --diff
options.description: Report only findings on lines added/modified by this unified diff. Pass a path to a diff file, or '-' to read the diff from stdin. Findings in the touched files that fall outside the changed lines are counted on stderr; add --diff-context to report them. Mutually exclusive with --git-ref.

options.name: --git-ref
options.description: Report only findings on lines changed in this git ref range (e.g. main..HEAD); runs 'git diff <range> --unified=0'. A two-dot range is diffed from the merge base (git's three-dot form) so commits that landed on the base branch since the branch point are not counted as your changes; an explicit three-dot range is used as typed, and a bare ref or SHA keeps git's meaning of 'working tree against that commit'. Findings in the touched files that fall outside the changed lines are counted on stderr; add --diff-context to report them. Mutually exclusive with --diff.

options.name: --diff-context
options.description: With --diff/--git-ref, also report findings in the touched files whose reported line is not among the changed lines — a class-level finding such as a newly introduced God-class, for example. They join the reported findings and the --fail-on gate. Without this flag they are only counted on stderr. [default: False]

options.name: --write-baseline
options.description: Run the analysis and write the current findings' fingerprints to this baseline file, then exit without reporting findings or failing. Use the file later with --baseline to gate only on new findings.

options.name: --baseline
options.description: Suppress findings recorded in this baseline file so output and --fail-on apply only to new findings. A missing file analyzes everything (with a warning). Generate the file with --write-baseline.

options.name: --telemetry
options.description: Enable opt-in telemetry: after the run, send one anonymous usage event (tool name, latency bucket, per-rule finding counts, hashed workspace id) to the CodeCharter endpoint. Off by default; no source, paths, or code are ever sent. [default: False]

commands.name: coverage
commands.description: Run tests with coverage collection and gate on a minimum line-coverage percentage. Exit codes: 0 = coverage met, 1 = below threshold, 2 = tests failed or coverage incomplete, 3 = no coverage data, 64 = usage, config or environment error.

options.name: --results-root
options.description: Directory where test and coverage artifacts are written. Defaults to <root>/TestResults/coverage. Relative paths resolve against the current working directory.

options.name: --skip-tests
options.description: Do not run 'dotnet test'; analyze existing coverage.cobertura.xml files under the results root instead. Completeness is checked per test project against the <results-root>/<project>-<hash> directories written by this command (plain <project> directories from older runs also count); a flat layout, e.g. from 'dotnet test --results-directory', degrades the check to comparing file and project counts. [default: False]

options.name: --output-file
options.description: Write the JSON coverage report to this file instead of stdout.

options.name: --min-coverage
options.description: Minimum required line-coverage percentage (0-100). Overrides the coverage.minimum-percent value from .codecharter/config.yml / config.local.yml; the built-in default is 100.

options.name: --git-ref
options.description: Gate the lines changed in this git ref range (e.g. main..HEAD or origin/main..HEAD) instead of the whole repository; runs 'git diff <range> --unified=0'. A two-dot range is diffed from the merge base (git's three-dot form) so commits that landed on the base branch since the branch point are not counted as your changes; an explicit three-dot range is used as typed, and a bare ref or SHA keeps git's meaning of 'working tree against that commit'. The report gains a 'diffCoverage' section and the exit code follows the diff gate. A diff without a single measurable changed line passes.

options.name: --affected-by
options.description: Run only the test projects reachable, by reverse ProjectReference closure, from the git range's changed files, instead of every discovered test project. Requires --git-ref naming the exact same range; incompatible with --skip-tests. A changed file that maps to no project, or to a central file (Directory.Build.props, a .sln, .codecharter/config.yml, build/**, .github/workflows/**, tools/**, ...), escalates the run back to every discovered test project. After the run, a changed source file with no coverage data at all fails the run and names the file: --affected-by never lets a narrower suite selection render as a passing gate over data it never measured.

options.name: --min-diff-coverage
options.description: Minimum required coverage of the changed lines (0-100). Requires --git-ref; without it the effective --min-coverage value is used for the diff gate as well.

options.name: --max-parallel
options.description: How many test projects may run at once after the shared solution build (1 or more). Defaults to the processor count, capped at 4. Overrides the coverage.max-parallel-test-projects value from .codecharter/config.yml / config.local.yml. Use 1 to serialise the runs, which tells a genuine failure apart from two projects contending on the same port, pipe or file. Ignored when there is no shared build, because concurrent per-project builds would race.

options.name: --test-timeout
options.description: How long a single test project may run, in seconds (1 to 86400). Defaults to 1800 (30 minutes). On expiry the test process and everything it started are killed and the project is reported as timed out; the run continues with the remaining projects. Bounds one project, not the whole run.

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Also print informational pipeline diagnostics ('info: …' lines) to stderr. By default only warnings and errors are shown. [default: False]

options.name: --no-color
options.description: Disable ANSI color codes [default: False]

options.name: --findings
options.description: Additionally render every uncovered region as a finding, through the same output formatters the 'analyze' verb uses. Severity follows the gate: info when the threshold is met, error when it is not. Purely additive — the JSON coverage report and the exit code are unchanged. [default: False]

options.name: --findings-file
